Maria Chen: Hey team — escalated from a customer: on-prem installer failing to fetch model shards and pip deps from worker nodes behind corp egress proxy. Works from bastion, fails from node.

Maria Chen: ```
[download] https://models.redwood.prod/cache/shard-0001.bin -> curl: (56) SSLRead() return error -9806
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "installer.py", line 212, in download_shard
    resp = requests.get(url, stream=True, timeout=30)
requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: TLSV1_ALERT_PROTOCOL_VERSION] tlsv1 alert protocol version (_ssl.c:1123)
```

Sam Ortiz: Can you run curl -v and openssl s_client from the failing host and paste output? Also confirm if the egress is via NAT GW or an intercepting outbound proxy.

Maria Chen: Curl shows TLS handshake failure; openssl s_client shows "No peer certificate" and sslv3 alert handshake failure.

Maria Chen: ```
$ curl -v https://models.redwood.prod/cache/shard-0001.bin
* Connected to models.redwood.prod (10.20.5.34) port 443
* TLS handshake error: tlsv1 alert handshake failure
curl: (35) error:14094416:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert handshake failure
```

Maria Chen: ```
$ openssl s_client -connect models.redwood.prod:443 -servername models.redwood.prod
CONNECTED(00000003)
140...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
No peer certificate available
---
```

Ryan Kline: That looks like TLS interception or SNI rewrite. If the corp proxy terminates TLS and re-signs certs, some clients (requests/OpenSSL) reject the chain or ALPN mismatch. Two asks: confirm egress path (transparent proxy vs NAT) and check proxy TLS logs for requests to models.redwood.prod, auth.redwood.prod, files.pythonhosted.org.

Sam Ortiz: If transparent proxy is doing SNI inspection you need SNI passthrough or exceptions for our hosts. Otherwise client cert validation fails.

Maria Chen: Customer says it's a transparent TLS-intercepting proxy that can't be disabled. They asked what minimal allowlist we need to avoid breaking installer/runtime.

Ryan Kline: Minimal FQDNs (include CDNs): models.redwood.prod, registry.redwood.prod, auth.redwood.prod, telemetry.redwood.prod, files.pythonhosted.org, pypi.org, cdn.python.org, storage.googleapis.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, huggingface.co, cdn-lfs.huggingface.co, artifacts.redwood.prod
Also require TLS passthrough for these hosts or proxy to present certs that include the original SANs.

Sam Ortiz: Also allow OCSP/CRL access (outbound TCP/UDP) since blocking OCSP can break cert validation. If passthrough impossible, proxy must forward OCSP correctly or cache responses.

Kevin Patel: I'll draft a KB with a minimal allowlist + checks: outbound 443 allowed, no TLS MITM for listed hosts, DNS resolves to public IPs, add hostname exceptions if proxy supports.

eng-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-8312. Please attach tcpdump and openssl logs. @Maria Chen @Sam Ortiz

Maria Chen: I'll send KB + logs to customer and ask network team for either TLS-exempt list or egress IP ranges. Will follow up with their tcpdump and proxy logs.

Maria Chen: Repro commands we asked them to run:
- curl -v https://models.redwood.prod/cache/shard-0001.bin
- openssl s_client -connect models.redwood.prod:443 -servername models.redwood.prod
- openssl s_client -connect files.pythonhosted.org:443 -servername files.pythonhosted.org -status
- sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 'tcp port 443 and host models.redwood.prod' -c 200

Maria Chen: They also saw OCSP responder timeouts to files.pythonhosted.org. Proxy blocks UDP to OCSP responders which caused cert validation timeouts in pip.

Ryan Kline: Add note: if corporate policy forbids passthrough, they must configure the proxy to not MITM these hostnames or to include original hostnames in re-signed cert SANs and allow OCSP checks to succeed.

Kevin Patel: Will circulate KB and close the loop after network confirms changes. :thumbsup:
